title: What My Girl Scout Daughter Taught Me About DTC Marketing
subtitle: Featuring Quinn and your ability to buy Girl Scout cookies.
body_html:
My daughter joined the Girl Scouts, and my son joined the Cub Scouts, but he didn't last very long. Quinn, on the other hand, and in part due to the relentless focus the Girl Scouts have on making sure everybody learns about direct to consumer marketing…has really blossomed. She has Girl Scout cookies to sell, and today's article is an interview with Quinn, and a call-to-action that lets you buy cookies from Quinn.

I have to tell you, I have to nominate my daughter for the Forbes 10 under 10, if that was a thing. Except she's very rule abiding, so I don't know if she's gonna find herself at the helm of Theranos II, or anything.

At home, our daughter listens to her favorite podcast with her parents, which is the technology podcast Hard Fork, and her second favorite podcast is the Acquired podcast. When her grandmother asked her what her favorite episode of Acquired was, she mentioned the episode on Visa. I then asked Quinn how many sides to the market that Visa created were there, and her answer was “A Lot!” …she continued: “there are the customers, and the merchants, and the bank of the customer, and the bank of the merchant, there are so many sides! It's like five or six!”

Visa, is, in fact, a five sided market.

It's important to know that my daughter is nine years old.

Quinn has one further Question for her dad:

“Daddy, can you heavily edit that?”

Yes Quinn, of course I can. What follows is a (lightly) edited transcript of my interview with Quinn about Girl Scout cookies and it will close with the ability buy your Girl Scout cookies from Quinn’s link.

Buy Girl Scout Cookies From Quinn!

TFP: Quinn, I’m interviewing you about your Girl Scout cookies. And... And then I’ll edit it. Tell me about being a Girl Scout.

Quinn: Um, you, like, learn things?

TFP: Like what things?

Q: You learn how to sell cookies, and can learn how to, like, do many things, like, be an entrepreneur or anything.

TFP: Why do you like the Girl Scouts?

Q: Because, uh, it’s fun.

TFP: That’s a good reason.

Q: Also, it helps like understand brands and stuff. It helps you when you grow up.

TFP: How does it help you when you grow up?

Q: If you want to be an entrepreneur, like me.

TFP: What do the Girl Scouts teach you about entrepreneurship?

Q: Uh, why don’t you sell cookies?

TFP: Okay, so what have you learned from selling cookies? What helps you sell a good cookie?

Q: That you just be like, “I would you like to buy my cookies”

TFP: Are Girl Scout Cookies a strong brand.

Q: Yes.

TFP: What makes them a strong brand?

Q: They’re famous. Mm hmm.

TFP: What do you like about representing Girl Scout cookies when you’re selling to people?

Q: Um, I don’t know.

TFP: Do you think they have good margins?

Q: They sell the cookies for more than they make them for.

TFP: yes they do…

[interrupted]

Q: It’s called profits!

TFP: That’s right. How do you feel about supporting a not-for-profit organization that makes a profit on their cookies?

Q: The Girl Scouts are non-profit—they just makes our dues less with the cookies so everyone can join.

TFP: Do you feel proud to be associated with the Girl Scouts?

Q: Uh, yeah.

TFP: Do you think the cookies are good?

Q: I don’t really know. I tried one.

TFP: Oh, you don’t really like sweet things that much.

Q: Not really. I like the one that is sweet, though.

TFP: Which cookies are new this year?

Q: The new one is called Exploremores™.. or something like that.

TFP: There’s a brand new one this year?

Q: They keep innovating on their cookie selections.

TFP: What’s the classic?

Q: The thin mints. Everyone knows that. But everyone was getting s’mores though.

TFP: Oh, is that a new one?

Q: No, it’s an old one. And it doesn’t taste as good. Not compared to the Thin Mints.

Q: I don’t like thin mints, daddy.

TFP: Fair enough. So why should everyone buy their Girl Scout cookies from you?

Q: Because I’m important, and it’ll help the Girl Scouts. My brother used to be a Boy Scout. He doesn’t do it anymore.

TFP: Why did the Girl Scouts keep you engaged where your brother kind of fell out?

Q: Well, first of all, my brother is kinda lazy.

TFP: Okay, that isn’t nice — are the Girl Scouts just more engaging?

Q: Yeah, and it’s more famous. The Boy Scouts aren’t famous for selling anything.

TFP: That’s true. Do you think you could be famous for selling the most Girl Scout cookies?

Q: No. I’m not even close. The most is like a thousand cookies.

TFP: That’s a lot of cookies. What do you think people should know about Girl Scouts?

Q: I’m done.

TFP: You can’t be done yet! Do you have advice on which cookies people should select?

Q: I think it depends on what people want. Like if you like something chocolate — go with the adventurefuls. I feel like I don’t know all the names but there is definitely a gluten free one this year.

TFP: Any parting thoughts for people who want to buy your cookies?

Q: If you’ve ever tasted Girl Scout cookies, you’ll probably like any of them. But use your common sense — like if you don’t like lemon, don’t try the Lemon-Ups.

TFP: Common sense cookie ordering. Wise words.

Q: Yeah. And also — if you ever see a Girl Scout, always buy from them.

TFP: Strong close, Quinn.
